retouches.prompt: Pixel art illustration: a red knitted sweater sleeve with a ribbed cuff reaches in from the right and ends in a plain brown furry paw resting flat on the lower right corner of a lined paper document with grey paw prints, which lies on a green patterned runner on a wooden cottage table. Change ONLY that paw: repaint it as a wombat's front foot, stocky and broad, covered in coarse shaggy brown-grey fur (a dull grey-brown with darker pixel shading and a few paler grey-brown fur highlights), ending in four broad strong dark claws, short and thick, pressed flat against the paper, with a small dark leathery pad just visible at its side. It is an animal's front foot, not a glove, not a mitten, not a hand. Same pose, same size and same position: it comes out of the red ribbed cuff exactly where the brown paw did and rests on the paper exactly where it rested. Keep the red knitted sleeve and its ribbed cuff, the paper with its lines and grey paw prints, the green runner and the wooden table exactly as they are. Same 16-bit pixel art rendering at exactly the same fine pixel scale as the knit stitches of the sleeve, with visible pixel clusters and the same warm lantern-lit palette: no enlarged blocky pixels, no photographic fur, no smooth vector shading, no thick outlines. Change nothing else. No human, no fingers, no skin.
